To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prefrontal acetylcholine transients are associated with veridical signal discrimination, and that prefrontal BLD activation during veridical discrimination is associated with faster response times.

cholinergic transmits are observed during signal hits but not during signal misses, that these transients are not observed during consecutive signal hits, and that they are observed during signal-hit trials that are preceded by nonsignal events.

1) right prefrontal cortex is involved in veridical detection of signals; 2) right prefrontcal cholinergic activity is involved in veridal signal detection; 3) right prefrontocortical cholinergic activity increases only during veridical detection when the signal is followed by a non-signaling event; 4) right prefrontalcortical BOLD increases during veridical signal-detection when the signal is preceded by a non-signal event
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive operations that mediate the integration and utilization of external cues and internal representations.
the cognitive processes that mediate the integration and use of external cues in the control of behavior.
the neural and cognitive processes that support attention to cues, cue-evoked response generation, and the shift from one to the other.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prefrontal cortex is involved in the integration of internal representations and external cues in order to guide and initiate behavior.
the cholinergic system in the prefrontal cortex is involved in the integration of external and internal cues to initiate and guide the behavior of animals and humans.
the prefrontal choline release and BOLD activation in the rostral PFC are the neural substrates of cognitive operations supporting the integration of external and internal representations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cholinergic mechanism in the prefrontal cortex is a key player for cognitive flexibility.
cholinergic activity is involved in the initiation of a response to a cue, but not in the execution of that response.

cholinergic activity, measured in the PFC, is a critical mechanism for instigating shifts from a state in which the animal is attending to the environment, or monitoring, to one in which it is responding to a cue that is presented in that environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cholinergic system in the prefrontal cortex is a key player in the cognitive operations underlying attentional control.

prefrontal cholinegic mechanisms are important for the integration of external signals (cues) with internal representations (e.g., response rules) to instigate shifts from monitoring for cues to cue-guided performance.
the prefrontal choline system is involved in the initiation and guidance of behavior.
